Aerial Wildlife Survey Report 
Wildlife Management Unit 306 Aerial Ungulate Survey (2025) 
Background 
WMU 306 is located northwest of Lundbreck, Alberta. 
It is bordered by highways 22 and 3, the Maycroft 
Road on the north and the Kananaskis road on the 
west. It consists of foothills and mountain habitats. 
WMU 306 has good quality habitat for moose, elk, and 
mule deer. WMU 306 was also surveyed specifically 
for elk in 2007,2015 and 2020. Past surveys did not 
calculate population densities or estimates for deer 
species or moose. 
Survey Method 
A rotary wing transect survey was conducted February 
12, 2025 flying 22 east-west lines at 1.85 km intervals, 
with 48 per cent coverage (800 m wide survey strip, 
area surveyed 180 km2) for a total linear survey effort 
of 224 km. At each observation point, ungulates were 
classified by species, and when possible, sex and age 
were recorded.  
Because transects varied in length, the average 
density (R) of mule deer, white-tailed deer, and moose 
was calculated by multiplying the number of animals 
per transect (Σx) by total area (km2) searched (total 
survey strip area [Σz]) (Jolly 1969, as described in 
Krebs 2014). Average density (R) was multiplied by 
the area (km2) WMU (Z) to determine population 
estimates with a 90 per cent confidence intervals. 
Confidence interval width was calculated by 
multiplying the t statistic for the left-tailed inverse of the 
Student’s t-distribution, (t0.05,df=n-1) by standard error 
(SE; without replacement) of the abundance estimate 
where SE= sq root variance, and variance = N*(N-n)/ 
(n*(n-1))*(Σx2+R2*ΣZ2-2*R*Σxz) with N as the total 
number of possible transects given 100 per cent 
coverage, and n as the number of transects sampled.  
Moose, deer and elk observations made during the 
survey were recorded even if outside of the transect 
width. Moose, mule deer and white-tailed deer data 
points were truncated to 800m strip width for 
population estimates. All elk observations were 
summed for a minimum total count.   
Results 
Mule Deer 
A total of 623 mule deer were observed on transect 
with an average group size of 11 (range 1-47). The 
estimated density was 3.47 mule deer/km2 and the 
estimated abundance was 1453 individuals (90 per 
cent CI 1116 – 1791). A total of 604 mule deer were 
successfully classified and the buck:doe:fawn ratio 
was calculated to be 44:100:41. Due to the timing of 
the survey being mid February, a small amount of 
antler drop had occurred which will affect these ratios. 
White-tailed Deer 
A total of 211 white-tailed deer were observed on 
transect with an average group size of 5.5 (range 1-
18). The estimated density was 1.17 deer/km2 and the 
estimated abundance was 492 individuals (90 per cent 
CI 361-623). White-tailed deer were not classified into 
sex and age cohorts due to extensive antler drop 
having occurred by the time the survey was 
conducted. The 2025 population estimate represents 
the only statistically rigorous method employed for 
white-tailed deer in WMU 306.  
Moose 
A total of 36 moose were observed on transect with 
and average group size of 1.86 (range 1-4). The 
estimated density was 0.2 moose/ km2 and the 
estimated abundance was 84 individuals (90 per cent 
CI 42-126). The bull:cow:calf ratio was found to be 
5:100:67. Moose were generally counted anecdotally 
in past surveys for a minimum total count, which likely 
greatly underestimated the population. 
Elk 
A
 total of 328 elk were observed with an average 
group size of 59 (range 1-242). The bull:cow:calf ratio 
was found to be 10:100:20. The past surveys are 
presented in Table 1. The elk population in 2025 is 
11% lower than that reported in 2020.
